77454.subject: Tether Passes Its First Full Audit, Keeps the Statements Private
77454.body:
**Hello, Defiers!**

* **[Tether](https://thedefiant.io/news/cefi/tether-clears-first-full-audit-from-kpmg-without-publishing-the-statements)**[ clears its first full audit in 12 years and publishes none of it](https://thedefiant.io/news/cefi/tether-clears-first-full-audit-from-kpmg-without-publishing-the-statements)

* **[Neutrl](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/neutrl-pauses-minting-and-redemptions-while-assessing-reserve-impact)**[ pauses minting and redemptions while it assesses its reserves](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/neutrl-pauses-minting-and-redemptions-while-assessing-reserve-impact)

* **[ether.fi](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/ether-fi-adds-tokenized-stocks-new-fiat-rails-and-aave-backed-borrowing)**[ adds tokenized stocks, fiat rails and Aave-backed borrowing to its app](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/ether-fi-adds-tokenized-stocks-new-fiat-rails-and-aave-backed-borrowing)

* **[Tempo](https://thedefiant.io/news/tradfi-and-fintech/tempo-earn-embedded-stablecoin-yield-deel)**[ launches embedded stablecoin yield for platforms, starting with Deel](https://thedefiant.io/news/tradfi-and-fintech/tempo-earn-embedded-stablecoin-yield-deel)

* **[SharpLink](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/sharplink-plans-200-million-eth-allocation-to-lido-s-wsteth)**[ plans a $200M ETH allocation to Lido's wstETH](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/sharplink-plans-200-million-eth-allocation-to-lido-s-wsteth)

**Read more below!**

———————————————————————————

———————————————————————————

##### PARTNER

———————————————————————————

##### WATCH

## How Robinhood Chain Hit 200M Transactions in 30 Days

**Robinhood Chain** went from zero to 200 million transactions in its first month. **Seong Lee**, who runs product for Robinhood Crypto, [walks Chris Storaker through what's driving the activity](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IMWBIaS7GIk), why its permissionless stock tokens can be redeemed even if Robinhood disappears, and where the yield in its insured DeFi lending product comes from.

Youtube: Robinhood's Head of Product Reveals How Robinhood Chain Hit 200M Transactions in 30 Days (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IMWBIaS7GIk)

———————————————————————————

##### CEFI

## Tether Clears First Full Audit From KPMG Without Publishing the Statements

Tether said **KPMG US** [issued an unqualified opinion](https://thedefiant.io/news/cefi/tether-clears-first-full-audit-from-kpmg-without-publishing-the-statements) on the 2025 accounts of **Tether International, S.A. de C.V.**, its El Salvador issuing entity — the first full financial-statement audit in the company's history. The work was performed to **AICPA** standards; the GENIUS Act sets **PCAOB** standards for licensed US issuers. Tether has released neither the statements nor the opinion letter.

**Why this matters:** A full audit was the longest-running demand on Tether. Meeting it on softer standards with the documents withheld moves the question from whether an audit exists to what it shows.

##### DEFI

# Thursday links: Bigfoot, re-rolling elections, North Korea, Gen Z investing

[Sasquatch science](https://aeon.co/essays/the-surprisingly-scientific-methods-of-bigfooters)

A study of the Bigfoot-hunting community finds that the search has taken an unexpected turn: “A field that has long been dominated by hunters and outdoorsmen is today also inhabited by a form of ‘citizen scientist’, armed with a pipette rather than a rifle.” 

The authors add that many Bigfooters are “dedicated empiricists who employ methodologies modeled on those found in professional scientific research.”

For an example of the empirical Bigfooter’s mindset, the authors quote the cryptozoologist George Eberhart: “You can apply a scientific method, or a journalistic method to it, to get some good science out of it.”

(I was disappointed to learn that a “cryptozoologist” is not a person who studies crypto enthusiasts, but a person who searches for and studies hidden, legendary, or unverified animals.) 

Bigfooters recognize that their science remains speculative. “There’s plenty of evidence, there’s no proof,” Cliff Barackman told the authors. “There’s a big difference.”

The evidence includes witness testimony, casts of footprints, recorded audio, and even the occasional photograph (the most famous of which is above). 

Some in the community argue that the only conclusive proof that Bigfoot exists would be a body — which makes killing a Bigfoot a scientific necessity.

Most are against the idea, reasoning that since the number of remaining Bigfoot is unknown, killing just one “may doom their population.”

Suspected hair samples have been tested for mysterious DNA. Suspected handprints have been analyzed for distinctive skin oil. “The results have been inconclusive so far.”

“Bigfooting is clearly empirical,” the authors conclude. “We hope readers of this essay, and of our [book](https://www.routledge.com/Bigfooters-and-Scientific-Inquiry-On-the-Borderlands-of-Legitimate-Science/Lewis-Bartlett/p/book/9781032777832), appreciate how seriously Bigfooters take this dimension of their work, even in the face of derision.”

 Back in the days when Afghanistan was still a ramshackle democracy, I visited a hospital in Kabul. The city was then enduring regular terrorist attacks by the Taliban. A suicide bomber had blown up a bus full of judges and court staff. One victim was married to a nurse, who was on duty when he arrived, horribly injured. (He is now paraplegic.) She was “coping”, a colleague told me, adding: “She’s one tough woman.”


 It is now five years since President Joe Biden pulled American troops out of Afghanistan. The Taliban swept to power immediately, overthrowing the elected government as soon as American protection was withdrawn.
